job.description:

This role sits within a well-established People & Culture team that supports a national workforce through a combination of operational HR support, employee relations guidance and strategic people projects. This position is ideal for a confident HR generalist who enjoys balancing day-to-day advisory work with meaningful people initiatives and organisational improvement projects.

The Role

Reporting to the HR Manager, you will:

  • Provide trusted HR advice across performance management, workplace conduct, leave management, wellbeing matters and policy interpretation.
  • Act as a key contact for employee relations matters, supporting managers with grievances, conflict resolution, disciplinary processes and workplace concerns.
  • Interpret and apply employment legislation, Enterprise Agreement provisions and organisational policies.
  • Support workforce planning initiatives and provide general HR advice across the employee lifecycle.
  • Lead and contribute to people projects across employee engagement, capability development, onboarding, culture and inclusion.
  • Assist with the review, development and implementation of HR policies, frameworks and programs.
  • Work closely with learning and development initiatives, including supporting learning management systems and training programs.
  • Contribute to employee surveys, engagement action plans, leadership capability frameworks and broader organisational development initiatives.
  • Provide first-level advice on HR queries while partnering with specialist teams for more complex payroll, recruitment and systems matters.

About You

You are a proactive HR professional who enjoys operating as a true generalist and is confident providing advice across both operational and project-based people initiatives.

You'll bring:

  • 5+ years' experience in a Human Resources Advisor, Senior HR Officer or similar generalist HR position.
  • Strong employee relations capability, including performance management, workplace conduct, grievances and policy interpretation.
  • Sound knowledge of Fair Work legislation, Enterprise Agreements and contemporary HR practices.
  • Experience supporting workforce projects, employee engagement initiatives or organisational development programs.
  • The ability to build credibility with stakeholders and provide practical, considered HR advice.
  • Strong written communication skills with experience preparing policies, reports and HR documentation.
  • Exposure to learning management systems and learning & development programs will be highly regarded.
  • Previous experience within government, statutory authorities, education, not-for-profit or similarly regulated environments will be advantageous.

Why Apply?

  • Join a growing national organisation with significant workforce expansion planned.

job.title: Senior Policy Planner
job.description:
About the organisation

The organisation operates within the government sector, focusing on policy planning and development in New Zealand.

About the role

As a Senior Policy Planner, you will lead policy research, analysis, and development to support Council decision-making under the Local Government Act and Resource Management Act. You will draft and review planning policies, guidelines, strategies, and technical reports, respond to District Plan enquiries, and prepare robust evidence for hearings and statutory processes.

Key responsibilities

  • Lead and manage policy planning projects, researching and amending key components of the District Plan.
  • Prepare high-quality planning reports, strategies, briefs, and evidence for Council, ensuring statutory timeframes and quality standards are met.
  • Apply the Resource Management Act and related legislation to provide robust policy advice and support effective plan administration.
  • Contribute towards the resource management reform programme and the Council's response.
  • Drive continuous improvement of policy planning systems and processes.
  • Build strong relationships with internal teams, consultants, stakeholders, and the community.

Skills & experience

  • Proven experience in policy planning, including a minimum of 5 years' practical experience applying the Resource Management Act 1991.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to present complex planning matters effectively.
  • Experience in preparing high-quality reports and briefings for diverse stakeholders.
  • Familiarity with GIS for analysis and mapping.
  • Ability to work with ambiguity and navigate complex policy issues.

Te whiwhinga mahi | The Opportunity

Join a territorial authority in one of Aotearoa New Zealand's most spectacular settings, where services, facilities and programmes are essential to the health and wellbeing of people and environment. This is a full-time, permanent opportunity based in Queenstown, within a high performing Planning & Development directorate. No two days are the same in New Zealand's fastest growing district.

He aha koe e whiwhi ai? | What's in it for you?

A dynamic and diverse community setting where your work makes a genuine difference every day.

$116,500 to $121,500 salary package

Southern Cross Wellbeing One Plan (full-time, permanent only)

Discounted membership to health and fitness facilities

Hybrid working practices

Genuine commitment to your training and career development

Kōrero mō te tūranga | About the Role

As a Senior Policy Planner you'll lead policy research, analysis and development that supports Council decision-making under the Local Government Act, Resource Management Act and the new planning reforms. You'll draft and review planning policies, guidelines, strategies, plan changes and technical reports, respond to District Plan enquiries, and prepare robust evidence for hearings and statutory processes. You'll help progress "Plan Stop" Variations granted exemptions to facilitate efficient development, alongside Private Plan Change requests with real project management scope. With continued high growth, the policy team is delivering policy development under the RMA — including giving effect to the NPS UD — while preparing for the reform programme.

Ngā kawenga | Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and manage policy planning projects, including researching, developing and amending key components of the District Plan
  • Prepare high-quality planning reports, strategies, briefs and evidence for Council, hearings and the Environment Court
  • Meet statutory timeframes and quality standards across all policy work
  • Apply the Resource Management Act and related legislation soundly and practically to provide robust policy advice
  • Support effective plan administration and respond to District Plan enquiries
  • Contribute to the RM reform programme and how the Council responds to it
  • Drive continuous improvement of policy planning systems, processes and service delivery
  • Build strong, collaborative relationships with internal teams, consultants, stakeholders and the wider community

Ngā pūkenga me ngā wheako | Skills & Experience

  • Tertiary qualification in planning or a related discipline, with membership of (or eligibility for) the New Zealand Planning Institute
  • Practical experience applying the Resource Management Act 1991 and associated legislation, with policy planning experience and consenting exposure an advantage
  • Proven involvement in district plan reviews or other planning policy projects within a New Zealand local government setting
  • Experience and confidence presenting at hearings as an expert planner
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, presenting complex planning matters to the public, professionals and decision-makers
  • Experience using GIS for analysis and mapping, and comfort working with ambiguity and evolving policy direction

Me pēhea te tuku tono | How to Apply

Apply online today and we'll keep you updated on progress. Applications are reviewed and processed as they come through, so early application is encouraged.

job.title: Policy Analyst
job.description:
Te whiwhinga mahi | The Opportunity

A rare chance to join a team sitting at the centre of investment decision making in the education system. The team runs the annual Budget process end to end — from developing the Budget Strategy through to delivering the education package on Budget Day. It's high-profile work, internally, for Ministers and within the education sector.

He aha koe e whiwhi ai? | What's in it for you?

  • Salary range $75,815 – $91,347 per annum plus KiwiSaver, with appointment reflecting your individual skills and experience
  • Full-time secondment of up to 5 months, Wellington-based
  • Flexible working arrangements where everyone feels valued and supported
  • The ability to purchase extra days leave
  • A range of employee network groups
  • An inclusive environment that encourages your personal cultural competency journey
  • Development and learning, including mentorship programmes and internal secondments
  • Wellness initiatives to support your overall health and wellbeing

Kōrero mō te tūranga | About the Role

You'll guide and advise on education priorities for the annual Budget process, building a picture of Government and organisational priorities, scanning the environment, and understanding cost pressures and their drivers. You'll advise on the inevitable trade-offs between initiatives in a contested and scaled process, and help shape a coherent package where no single initiative sits in isolation. Along the way you'll build a sound understanding of the Vote, current expenditure and public finance processes. There's also real scope to grow your presentation and coaching skills by training and supporting other teams through the Budget process.

Ngā kawenga | Key Responsibilities

  • Guide and advise on education priorities for the annual Budget process
  • Build an understanding of Government and organisational priorities and needs, including environmental scanning
  • Analyse cost pressures and their drivers
  • Ensure the fit of education priorities within the overall Government strategic and policy direction for Budget
  • Advise on trade-offs between initiatives in a contested and scaled process
  • Help shape a coherent package of initiatives
  • Build a sound understanding of the Vote, current expenditure and drivers, and public finance processes
  • Work with other teams to provide training and support through the Budget process

Ngā pūkenga me ngā wheako | Skills & Experience

  • Good knowledge of policy processes, with experience in a relevant policy role
  • Qualifications in a relevant discipline such as public policy, economics or finance, or equivalent professional experience
  • Good numeracy skills and confidence working in Excel
  • Strong relationship management and communication skills across diverse teams and agencies
  • The ability to think clearly through problems and to manage and deliver on multiple priorities
  • Knowledge of, or a willingness to gain an understanding of, Te Ao Māori, tikanga, te reo Māori and te Tiriti o Waitangi as it applies in the public sector, along with the Public Service Standards of Integrity and Conduct

Big 4 Opportunity – Corporate & International Tax Associate / Senior Associate

Brisbane CBD | Top-Tier Consulting Firm | Work with Leading Multinationals

We are excited to be partnering with one of the world’s most prestigious top-tier professional services firms to recruit a Corporate & International Tax Associate / Senior Associate for their Brisbane team. The position offers exposure to both compliance and advisory work, allowing you to develop strong technical capability while building trusted relationships with clients.

  • Working with large Australian corporates and multinational groups across multiple industries

You will also benefit from working directly with senior tax leaders who are recognised experts in the field, giving you exposure that few roles can offer at this stage of your career.

About You

  • We are keen to speak with candidates who have: 1–4 years’ experience in Australian Corporate Tax within a Big 4 or mid-tier firm

  • Strong attention to detail and analytical thinking
  • A genuine interest in developing deeper technical tax expertise
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively
  • CA / CPA / CTA (completed or in progress), or a similar qualification

job.title: Chief Executive Officer
job.description:
Chief Executive Officer

Lead the Peak Body for Australia's Strata and Community Titles Sector Strata Community Association (SCA) is the peak industry body representing strata and community title professionals across Australia and New Zealand. Through advocacy, education, professional standards and member engagement, SCA plays a critical role in shaping the future of one of Australia's most significant and rapidly evolving property sectors. Reporting to the Board through the President, the Chief Executive Officer will lead the organisation through its next phase of growth, influence and organisational capability. This is an opportunity for an accomplished executive leader to shape industry outcomes, strengthen member value and drive the strategic direction of a respected national membership organisation.

About the Role

The CEO is responsible for translating Board-approved strategy into disciplined operational delivery while ensuring strong governance, financial sustainability and organisational performance. The role requires sound commercial judgement, political awareness, governance maturity and the ability to lead across a complex national stakeholder environment.

Working closely with the Board, Corporate Members, Chapters, government stakeholders, regulators, sponsors and industry partners, you will:

  • Lead the execution of SCA's strategic plan and annual business priorities
  • Provide high-quality governance support, reporting and strategic advice to the Board
  • Drive financial sustainability and commercial performance across events, sponsorships, education and member services
  • Build trusted relationships across SCA's national federated membership structure
  • Lead advocacy, policy and government engagement initiatives
  • Strengthen professional standards, education and accreditation programs across the sector
  • Develop organisational capability, leadership succession and workforce planning
  • Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration and operational excellence
  • Represent SCA as the trusted and credible national voice for the strata and community titles sector

Key Selection Criteria

To be considered for this opportunity, you will demonstrate:

  • Significant senior executive leadership experience within an industry association, professional body, member organisation, not-for-profit or similarly complex stakeholder environment
  • Proven experience reporting to and working closely with a Board
  • Experience leading within a federated, chapter-based or multi-jurisdictional structure
  • Strong commercial and financial management capability, including budgeting, forecasting and oversight of commercial activities
  • A track record of translating strategy into measurable outcomes through disciplined execution and accountability
  • Outstanding stakeholder management and relationship-building skills
  • Strong judgement, political awareness and the ability to operate effectively within delegated authority
  • Exceptional communication, influencing and leadership capabilities
  • Personal resilience, accountability and a commitment to ethical leadership
  • Experience within industry associations, professional bodies, membership organisations or regulated environments will be highly regarded
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications and/or governance credentials, are also desirable

Applications are invited from accomplished executive leaders with strong governance, financial and stakeholder management capabilities, and proven experience leading in complex stakeholder environments. You will bring sound judgement, resilience and accountability, together with the ability to translate strategy into outcomes and lead through clarity, influence and delivery.

An attractive executive remuneration package, including performance-based incentives, will be negotiated with the successful candidate.

Applications close Friday 14 August.

We're looking for a commercially savvy Category Manager who understands what makes passionate fans tick. This is your chance to combine your love of gaming, hobbies and collectibles with serious commercial responsibility, taking ownership of an established category within a fast-moving online retail business.

He aha koe e whiwhi ai? | What’s in it for you?

Turn your passion for the products into a career where you can make a genuine commercial impact, with a business that values performance and internal progression.

$100,000–$120,000 base salary plus performance-based bonus

Flexible start and finish times

Subsidised health insurance and free onsite parking

Staff discounts, product allowances and subscription benefits

Annual learning and development budget

Daily breakfast, fruit and snacks

Paid volunteer day, EAP, annual flu shots and team social activities

Opportunities for performance-based salary reviews and internal progression

Kōrero mō te tūranga | About the Role

Imagine being the person deciding which trading card releases, tabletop games, model kits and must-have collectibles make it into the range – and having the commercial ownership to back those decisions.

You'll take the lead on an established Hobbies & Collectibles portfolio, shaping the product strategy, building relationships with specialist suppliers and staying ahead of the releases, trends and communities that drive demand.

But this isn't just about knowing your Pokémon from your Warhammer. You'll own the numbers too – driving revenue, margins, stock performance and profitability, while making smart decisions about where to invest and when to move.

It's a great opportunity for someone who loves the category but also gets a genuine buzz from negotiating a great deal, spotting a commercial opportunity and seeing their strategy deliver results.

Ngā kawenga | Key Responsibilities

  • Own and execute category strategies to grow revenue, market share and profitability.

  • Develop product ranges, optimise SKU performance and identify growth opportunities.
  • Lead supplier negotiations, secure product allocations and improve trading terms.
  • Drive demand forecasting, inventory planning, stock turn and aged stock reduction.
  • Plan and execute promotional campaigns, product launches and pre-order strategies.
  • Analyse trading performance, customer trends and competitor activity to guide decisions.
  • Partner with marketing, merchandising, logistics and demand planning teams to deliver commercial outcomes.

Ngā pūkenga me ngā wheako | Skills & Experience

  • Proven end-to-end category management experience within retail or eCommerce, including independent commercial and P&L accountability.
  • Demonstrated success improving revenue, margins, profitability, inventory performance and supplier outcomes.
  • Experience in hobbies, collectibles, toys, gaming or trading card games is highly advantageous; consumer electronics or broader retail backgrounds are also welcome.
  • Strong supplier relationship management, negotiation and commercial decision-making skills.
  • Advanced Excel and analytical capability, with confidence using data to drive forecasting, range and inventory decisions.
  • An owner's mindset, proactive working style and genuine enthusiasm for niche, community-driven product categories.

If you know your way around a P&L as well as you know your favourite games, hobbies or collectibles, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply online today and we'll keep you updated on progress.

  • Proven experience leading large-scale (around $20 million), complex technology transformation programs with accountability for end-to-end delivery outcomes.

  • Demonstrated experience delivering programs through systems integrators and multi-vendor environments.

The Opportunity:

Join people2people Recruitment an award-winning recruitment and outsourcing partner with a standout culture and a track record of delivering results. We’re looking for an experienced Talent Acquisition Lead to run end to end hiring in a fast-paced client environment under a RPO/CMO model. Why people2people:

Winner of RCSA Outstanding Large Agency Award 2025, 2024, 2023 and continuing to grow from strength to strength.
